name: P-RAG: Progressive Retrieval Augmented Generation For Planning on Embodied Everyday Task
venue: ACM MM 2024 (Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Multimedia); DOI 10.1145/3664647.3680661; also arXiv:2409.11279
authors_affiliation: Weiye Xu (University of Science and Technology of China, USTC), Min Wang (Institute of Artificial Intelligence, Hefei Comprehensive National Science Center), Wengang Zhou (USTC), Houqiang Li (USTC). Hefei, China.
task_domain: embodied (embodied everyday task planning / instruction-following action sequencing from language goal + visual observation)
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent embodied planning where an LLM agent must output a sequence of high-level actions to complete an everyday task given a natural-language goal instruction and per-step visual observations (converted to scene graphs). Crucially the setting is WITHOUT ground-truth action demonstrations: unlike prior LLM-Planner-style few-shot methods that use GT trajectories as in-context examples, P-RAG only uses trajectories the agent itself generates through environment interaction. Operates over rounds/iterations across a set of tasks: round 1 builds the database from raw interaction, later rounds retrieve and write back. Weak/no supervision (reward + done signal from environment, no GT labels).
what_is_retrieved: Past interaction experiences stored as 4-tuples per task trajectory: goal instruction, scene graph (observation), history (sequence of (action, observation) pairs), and the 'done' completion state from a previous round's interaction.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes (a dynamic trajectory database progressively built and updated across rounds from the agent's own interactions); no static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K ranking objective: P-RAG selects the top-K database entries by a composite cosine-similarity score (goal-instruction similarity + max scene-graph/situation similarity). No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (similarity retrieval of past trajectories), Reuse (injected as experiential reference into the LLM prompt), Retain (write-back of new trajectories into the database each round). Revise is NOT explicitly implemented as a case-adaptation step (no critic/revision of the retrieved case itself). Flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: no, Retain: yes]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for planning and does not cite or use case-based reasoning terminology (no Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner); it realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under the RAG framing.
retrieval_unit: Full task trajectory tuple: (goal instruction, scene graph, history of (A_t, O_t) pairs, done state). Retrieval is keyed on two granularities — whole-task (goal) and per-situation (scene-graph) — but the retrieved/returned unit is a complete past task trajectory.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The database is initialized empty, constructed in the first round purely from agent-environment interaction, and progressively updated each subsequent round with the latest trajectories. No offline corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index keyed by embeddings, stored as a key-value store: 384-dim MiniLM embeddings (in JSON) for goal instruction and scene graph serve as keys; raw trajectory text content stored in a SQLite database (~3.2KB/task). No graph or hierarchical organization.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf sentence embeddings via MiniLM) with cosine similarity; composite score combining goal-instruction similarity and max situation/scene-graph similarity.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a frozen pretrained MiniLM encoder with cosine similarity; the retriever itself is not trained or fine-tuned on any similarity/effectiveness signal. (Note: the overall system 'learns' across rounds only by growing the database, not by training the retriever.)
query_construction: Raw input embedding: the current goal instruction I_g and the current observation O_t (passed through a scene-graph extraction module F) are each encoded with MiniLM into query vectors Q_goal and Q_obs,t. No query decomposition/expansion/intent extraction.
query_granularity: Two-level retrieval: task-level (goal instruction query) AND step/situation-level (scene-graph query, with a max over the t situations in each stored trajectory). The paper calls this a 'more granular retrieval scheme' retrieving both similar tasks and similar situations.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative across rounds with a fixed schedule within an episode: from round 2 onward, retrieval is performed at each step's interaction (per step the current goal+observation query the database). The 'progressive' aspect is iterative re-retrieval against an ever-growing database across rounds; within a round it is on a fixed per-step schedule, not uncertainty/router-triggered.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule, conditioned only on database non-emptiness: if DB is non-empty (i.e., after round 1), retrieve and augment; in round 1 (empty DB) the agent plans from LLM prior + observation alone. No confidence/attention/learned-classifier/reflection trigger.
reranking: None. Items are scored by the composite similarity (Eq. 3) and top-K selected directly; no cross-encoder / hierarchy-aware / RRF reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: Light selection only: top-K by composite similarity score, then formatted into text and concatenated into the prompt. For MINI-BEHAVIOR, scene-graph relation matrices are pruned to keep only 'true' pairs to reduce context length. No decompose/distill/distractor-filtering of retrieved cases.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; experiences are not tools).
index_content_separation: Yes (lightweight). Lightweight 384-dim embedding keys (goal + scene graph) are stored separately (JSON) from heavy raw trajectory content (text in SQLite, ~3.2KB/task) which is loaded on demand for the matched entries — a separation of index keys from heavy content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool API/protocol; the database is internally grown and updated each round via the agent's own trajectory write-back).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools / no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved top-K experiences (goal instruction, scene graph, history of (action,observation) pairs, done state) are converted to text and integrated into a single coherent prompt as 'experiential references' for the LLM planner alongside the current goal, observation (scene graph), and action space.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan, per-step interleaved within an iterative/progressive loop. At each step the agent retrieves relevant past trajectories from the growing DB and conditions the LLM's action generation on them; trajectories are written back after each round to improve subsequent rounds (one-shot exemplar-style augmentation at decision time, repeated progressively across rounds).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step (per action decision): retrieval augmentation feeds the LLM at each planning step within an episode; across rounds the database grows, but there is no per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar (no explicit case adaptation/revision): retrieved past trajectories are injected as in-context experiential references; the LLM is prompted to plan with them but there is no execution-feedback-driven or critic-guided revision of the retrieved case content.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw trajectory in text form: the surface form injected is the past goal instruction, scene graph, the sequence of (action, observation) pairs (history), and the done state, rendered as text. Not distilled into strategies/guidelines or executable skills.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory (low abstraction): complete past interaction histories with their success/failure 'done' flags, not distilled strategies, guidelines, or reusable workflows.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Minimal/implicit. The 'done' completion state accompanies each retrieved trajectory so the LLM can judge whether a referenced experience succeeded; similarity-based top-K selection and scene-graph pruning (keeping only true relations) reduce irrelevant context. No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or retriever-aware/distractor-aware training.
memory_type: episodic (a growing trajectory/experience database of past interactions, keyed by goal+scene-graph embeddings).
write_back: True. After each round/iteration completes (multiple tasks), the agent's new trajectories (goal instruction, scene graph, history, done state) are stored and the database is updated with the latest historical trajectory data.
online_growth: Yes. The retrievable database is initialized empty and grows/updates across rounds during deployment/test-time; in the 'Self-Iter.' variant it grows directly over the test set across iterations (up to ~6 iterations).
write_back_trigger: On-success-and-failure, end-of-round schedule: after each iteration (a full pass over the task set) the database is updated with that round's trajectories regardless of success — both successful and failed trajectories are stored (each tagged with its 'done' state). Write occurs per-round, not per-step, and is not gated on success or human validation.
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure stored: every stored trajectory carries a boolean 'done' (success/failure) state. Table 4's correlation analysis shows P-RAG leverages information from unsuccessful previous trajectories to achieve new successes (e.g., 6.8%-17.6% of False tasks flip to True in subsequent iterations), so failed experiences are retained and usable, not discarded.
memory_evolution_update: Refine-overwrite / append across rounds: each round the database is updated with the latest round's historical trajectory data for each task (the stored entry per task is replaced/refreshed with the most recent round's trajectory). The store grows across the task set and is progressively updated round to round; no dedup-merge, delta linking, or pruning is described.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is fixed top-K by frozen-embedding cosine similarity (composite goal + scene-graph score); it is not an RL/learned case-selection policy. System improvement comes from growing the memory, not from learning the retriever.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory; the database belongs to one agent/framework and is not shared across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: ALFRED (using ALFWORLD TextWorld tools to convert image observations to text; Train100 = 100 sampled training tasks following LLM-Planner, Valid Seen = 242 tasks, Valid Unseen = 85 tasks) and MINI-BEHAVIOR (20 activities/environments abstracted from BEHAVIOR-1K in a grid world).
baselines: On ALFRED: HiTUT, HLSM, E.T. (Episodic Transformer), M-TRACK (full-train methods); LLM-Planner, SayCan, and *HLSM (few-/partial-data methods); GPT-4 zero-shot baseline. On MINI-BEHAVIOR: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 zero-shot baselines (and reference to vanilla PPO from the MINI-BEHAVIOR paper, ~8% on a single task).
key_metrics: Success Rate (SR) on ALFRED Valid Seen / Valid Unseen; on MINI-BEHAVIOR: Total SR (success averaged by episodes), Task SR (success averaged by tasks), and SPL (Success weighted by Path Length).
headline_result: On ALFRED Valid Unseen, P-RAG (Self-Iter.) reaches 27.4% SR (up from the 7.05% GPT-4 zero-shot baseline) without using any ground-truth actions, outperforming all compared methods including full-training methods; the standard P-RAG (iterated on Train100) reaches 14.11% on Valid Unseen vs LLM-Planner's 12.92%.
ablations: 1) Progressive iteration (Table 3 / Fig. 5): ALFRED Valid Unseen SR climbs 7.05% (original) -> 14.11% (1st) -> 20.00% (2nd) -> 22.35% (3rd), saturating at 27.4% after ~5 self-iterations; Train100 5% -> 9% -> 10% -> 11%. 2) Scene-graph joint retrieval (Table 5): P-RAG with goal+scene-graph joint retrieval (14.11%) vs P-RAG w/o SG (task-name only, 13.10%) vs GPT-4 (7.05%), showing situation/scene-graph retrieval helps. 3) Cross-iteration correlation (Table 4): shows successes persist and some prior failures flip to success across iterations, attributing gains to use of failed-trajectory information. 4) LLM choice (Table 2): P-RAG improves over both GPT-4 (+1.7% Total SR) and GPT-3.5 (+2.5%) baselines on MINI-BEHAVIOR.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (SR / Total SR / Task SR / SPL) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome (success rate) metrics. SPL adds a path-efficiency dimension (process efficiency relative to shortest path) on MINI-BEHAVIOR, and Table 4 reports cross-iteration success-persistence as a process-level diagnostic, but there is no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported in terms of iterations/data efficiency rather than API cost/latency: up to 6 iterations max; performance saturates around 3-5 rounds. Uses ~1/200 of ALFRED training data (Train100 of 21,023) yet beats full-train methods on Valid Unseen. Storage ~3.2KB/task (SQLite) plus 384-dim embeddings. Contrasts with vanilla PPO (1e6 steps for ~8% on a single task). No explicit token-count, dollar-cost, or wall-clock latency numbers reported. [uncertain on exact per-query token/latency cost]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-K retrieved entries injected into the prompt (K not numerically specified in the paper text; the exact K value is [uncertain]). Context is reduced by converting observations to compact scene graphs and pruning MINI-BEHAVIOR relation matrices to true-only pairs. No explicit token budget cap stated.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-construction paper; it reuses ALFRED and MINI-BEHAVIOR). For reference: ALFRED Train100 = 100 of 21,023 tasks (stratified across 7 task types), Valid Seen = 242, Valid Unseen = 85; MINI-BEHAVIOR = 20 environments/activities from BEHAVIOR-1K.
builds_on: LLM-Planner (Song et al., 2023; retrieval-augmented LLM planning with GT few-shot for ALFRED) which it directly extends; uses GPT-4/GPT-3.5 as LLM planners; MiniLM (Wang et al., 2020) for embeddings; ALFWORLD/TextWorld (Cote et al., 2019) and ALFRED (Shridhar et al., 2020) for environments; MINI-BEHAVIOR / BEHAVIOR-1K (Jin et al., 2023); Fast Marching Method (Sethian, 1999) for high-level-to-low-level action decomposition; conventional one-shot RAG.
contrasts_with: Conventional one-shot RAG (retrieves once from a static database) — P-RAG instead progressively grows and re-retrieves an evolving database across rounds. LLM-Planner and SayCan — which rely on ground-truth action demonstrations / step-by-step instructions as few-shot samples, whereas P-RAG uses only self-generated interaction trajectories (no GT) and retrieves both similar tasks and similar situations. Full-supervision learning-based methods (HiTUT, HLSM, E.T., M-TRACK) that need the entire training set and extensive training.
lineage: Sub-topic C (RAG for planning / experience-memory-augmented embodied LLM planning): a progressive, growing-memory, write-back RAG planner for embodied everyday tasks; positioned between classic one-shot RAG planners (LLM-Planner) and later experience/case-memory planners, distinguished by ground-truth-free, iteratively-grown trajectory memory with two-level (task + situation) retrieval.
